correctness.rationale: Reconstructed parameter spaces directly from quadratic relations: dimension 15 in odd characteristic (9 degree-one, 3 degree-two inner, 3 degree-three) and 21 for radical-preserving derivations in characteristic 2. The radical-filtration diagonal blocks are \(B\), \((\operatorname{tr} B)I-B^*\) and \(\operatorname{tr} B\); hence the exact maximal-rank criterion. Two-kernel subspace Möbius inversion gives \(N(q)=q^3(q^5-2q^4-q^3+q^2+3q+2-\mathbf1_{\mathrm{char}=2})\); the full cardinalities follow from \((q-1)N(q)\) times \(q^6\) or \(q^{12}\). Standalone complete leading-matrix counts for \(q=2,3,4,5\) give 24,1998,30528,224000; derivation-space ranks and actual Leibniz/rank samples checked for p=2,3,5. Finite tests corroborate, not replace the infinite-field proof.

value.rationale: The Jacobson radical is canonical and seven is the maximal possible radical rank, so this counts a natural extremal stratum of ordinary derivations rather than arbitrary chosen coefficients. The arithmetic answer for all finite fields depends on both a dimension jump of six in characteristic two and a distinct trace-resonance correction of \(q^3\); the exact polynomial can be used as a probability of radical-bijectivity and as a small-rank benchmark for other exterior/truncated algebras. This is an exact natural invariant, not merely a finite sample or a restated general decomposition.
